chapters.title: Analytics
intro: This chapter is for supervisors and managers who track support performance. Agents can also use it to see their own numbers.
It covers dashboards, standard reports, drilling down to tickets, exporting and scheduled e-mail reports.

sections.title: What you see in Analytics
sections.intro: Select **Analytics** in the main menu. The numbers cover only the tickets you may see. The line under the title says which tickets are counted and which time zone is used.

rows: See your own tickets only. The page says **Personal analytics**.
See every ticket in your data scope, and share dashboards.
Export reports and use the **Exports** tab.
Schedule e-mailed reports and use the **Scheduled** tab.
Pages of charts and figures. Four come ready-made, and you can build your own.
Ten standard reports with figures, charts and tables.
Reports that are e-mailed on a schedule.
Files you exported, ready to download.

blocks.note: Times are business hours where a figure says (bh). Spam, merged and deleted tickets are never counted.

sections.title: Dashboards at a glance
sections.intro: The **Dashboards** tab opens the dashboard you used last.

blocks.caption: The Service performance dashboard for the last 30 days.
blocks.alt: Analytics dashboards tab with numbered highlights on the tabs, the dashboard list, the period and filter bar, Edit layout, the dashboard menu and a widget

callouts: The dashboard list. It groups dashboards under **Role defaults**, **Shared** and **Personal**.
The period, **Compare** and **Filters**. They apply to every widget on the page.
**Edit layout** lets you add, move and resize widgets.
The dashboard menu: **New dashboard**, **Duplicate as personal**, **Settings** and **Delete dashboard**.
A widget. Select its number to see the tickets behind it.

rows: Your open and resolved tickets, first response and CSAT.
Backlog, SLA compliance, agent scorecard and channels.
Resolution time, departments, escalations and backlog.
Demand, CSAT, products, top customers and tiers.

sections.title: Choose the period and filters
sections.intro: Change what the dashboard or report counts.
prerequisites: You have the **View personal dashboards and reports** permission.
steps: In the period list, choose a period, such as **Last 30 days**. Choose **Custom range** to enter your own dates.
To compare with an earlier period, turn on **Compare**. Then choose **Previous period** or **Same period last year**.

steps.caption: The Filters panel with the fields you can filter by.
steps.alt: Filters panel with Department, Team, Agent, Channel, Priority, Customer, Product and Tier, and Reset and Apply filters

steps: Choose one or more values in the fields you need, such as **Department** or **Priority**.
Select **Apply filters**.
sections.result: Every widget or report figure updates. Each active filter appears as a chip next to **Filters**.

blocks.tip: Select the cross on a chip to remove one filter. Select **Clear filters** to remove them all. **Reset** in the panel clears your choices before you apply them.

sections.title: See the tickets behind a number
sections.intro: Find out which tickets make up a figure, a bar or a row.
prerequisites: You have the **View personal dashboards and reports** permission.
steps: Open a dashboard or a report.
Select a figure, a bar, a point on a line or a table row.

steps.text: Read the list of tickets in the panel that opens.
steps.caption: The tickets behind the Tickets created figure.
steps.alt: Drill-down panel titled Tickets created with the period, ticket count and a list of tickets with status, assignee, customer, date, priority and SLA breached

steps: To see more, select **Load more** at the bottom.
Select a ticket to open it.
sections.result: The ticket opens. The panel shows the period and the number of tickets at the top.

blocks.note: **SLA breached** in red means the ticket missed an SLA target.

sections.title: Create your own dashboard
sections.intro: Build a dashboard with only the figures you need.
prerequisites: You have the **View personal dashboards and reports** permission.
steps: On the **Dashboards** tab, select the dashboard menu (**...**).
Select **New dashboard**.

steps.caption: The New dashboard dialog.
steps.alt: New dashboard dialog with Name, Description, Default period, the share switch, Cancel and Create dashboard

steps: Choose the **Default period**.
To let others see it, turn on **Share with everyone who has analytics access**.
Select **Create dashboard**.
Add widgets as described in [Add a widget to a dashboard](#analytics-add-widget).
sections.result: The new dashboard opens in edit mode. It appears under **Personal**, or under **Shared** when shared.

blocks.note: Only people with the **View team, department and organisation analytics** permission can share a dashboard.

blocks.tip: To start from a built-in dashboard, open it and select **Duplicate as personal** in the menu.

sections.title: Add a widget to a dashboard
sections.intro: A widget shows one measure as a figure, a chart or a table.
prerequisites: You can edit the dashboard. You can always edit your own personal dashboards.
steps: Open the dashboard and select **Edit layout**.
Select **Add widget**.

steps.caption: The Add widget dialog with a KPI widget and its preview.
steps.alt: Add widget dialog with Visualisation choices, Metric, Title, Period, the compare switch, widget filters, a preview, Cancel and Add widget

steps: In **Metric**, choose what to measure. Change the **Title** if you want.
For a chart or table, choose **Break down by** and **Show top**. For a table, add **More columns** if needed.
Leave **Period** on **Dashboard period**, or choose a fixed period.
Optionally, choose **Widget filters**. The app adds them to the page filters.
Check the preview, then select **Add widget**.
Select **Save layout**.
sections.result: The message **Dashboard saved** appears. The widget shows on the dashboard.

blocks.tip: In edit mode, each widget has arrow buttons to move it. **W−** and **W+** change its width. **H−** and **H+** change its height. The pencil edits it and the bin removes it.

blocks.note: Select **Cancel** in the toolbar to leave edit mode without saving your changes.

sections.title: Rename, share or delete a dashboard
sections.intro: Change a dashboard's details, or remove it when nobody needs it.
prerequisites: You can edit the dashboard. Role default dashboards cannot be deleted.
steps: Open the dashboard.
Select the dashboard menu (**...**), then **Settings**.
Change the **Name**, **Description**, **Default period** or sharing. Select **Save**.
To delete it, select **Delete dashboard** in the menu instead. Confirm with **Delete**.
sections.result: The dashboard shows its new details, or it disappears from the list.

blocks.warning: Deleting a shared dashboard removes it for everyone who can see it.

sections.title: Standard reports
sections.intro: Select the **Reports** tab. Select a report card to open it. There is no free-form report builder.

blocks.caption: The report library, grouped by topic.
blocks.alt: Reports tab with report cards grouped under Operations, Quality, People, Product and Customers

rows: Created against resolved, the backlog trend and how long open tickets have waited.
Median and 90th percentile first response and resolution times in business hours.
Compliance by milestone, breaches by priority and department, and the breach list.
First contact resolution, reopen and escalation rates by agent and category.
Volume, speed, first contact resolution, SLA and CSAT by channel.
CSAT trend, rating spread, CSAT by agent and the lowest-rated tickets.
Resolved tickets, replies, handle time, use of time and current workload per agent.
The categories and root causes behind most tickets, and repeated issues.
Tickets, breaches and reopens per product, module and version.
Tickets, open backlog, breaches, reopens and CSAT per customer, with a health score.

sections.title: Run a report
sections.intro: Open a standard report and set the period and filters you need.
prerequisites: You have the **View personal dashboards and reports** permission.
steps: Select **Analytics**, then the **Reports** tab.
Select a report, such as **SLA compliance**.
Choose the period, **Compare** and **Filters** as in [Choose the period and filters](#analytics-period-filters).
Read the line under the filter bar. It shows the dates, the comparison, the filters and the time zone.
Read the key figures, charts and tables.
sections.result: The report shows figures for the chosen period and filters.

blocks.caption: The SLA compliance report with its key figures and charts.
blocks.alt: SLA compliance report with numbered highlights on All reports, the filter bar, Schedule, Export and the key figures

callouts: **All reports** returns to the report library.
**Export** saves the report as a file.
The key figures. With **Compare** on, each shows the change against the comparison period.

sections.title: Export a report
sections.intro: Save a report as a file to share it or work on it in a spreadsheet.
steps: Open the report and set the period and filters.
Select **Export**.

steps.caption: The Export menu with the three file formats.
steps.alt: Export menu with Excel workbook, CSV and PDF document

steps: Wait for the message **Export ready**. The file downloads.
sections.result: The file is saved on your computer. It also appears on the **Exports** tab.

blocks.note: Large exports run in the background. The message **Export still running** appears. Download the file later from the **Exports** tab.

sections.title: Download an earlier export
sections.intro: Get a file that you exported before.
steps: Select **Analytics**, then the **Exports** tab.
Find the export. The list shows the **Report**, **Format**, **Status**, **Requested** time, **Rows** and **Size**.
When the status shows **Succeeded**, select **Download**.
When the status shows **Queued** or **Running**, wait. Then select **Refresh**.
sections.result: The file downloads to your computer.

sections.title: Schedule a report
sections.intro: Have a report e-mailed as an attachment every day, week or month.
prerequisites: You have the **Schedule report delivery** permission.
steps: Open the report and select **Schedule**. Or select **New schedule** on the **Scheduled** tab.

steps.caption: The Schedule a report dialog for the SLA compliance report.
steps.alt: Schedule a report dialog with Name, Report, Period covered, Compare with, Format, Department, Priority, Channel, Frequency, Day, Time, Time zone, Recipients, Active, Cancel and Create schedule

steps: Choose the **Period covered**, **Compare with** and **Format**.
Optionally, choose a **Department**, **Priority** or **Channel**.
Choose the **Frequency**: **Daily**, **Weekly** or **Monthly**. Then choose the **Day** or **Day of month**, and the **Time**.
Check the **Time zone**, such as `Asia/Kolkata`.
In **Recipients**, enter an e-mail address and press [[Enter]]. Repeat for up to 20 people.
Leave **Active** on, and select **Create schedule**.
sections.result: The message **Report scheduled** shows the next run. The schedule appears on the **Scheduled** tab.

blocks.note: The period is rolling. For example, **Last 7 days** always means the seven days before each run. The report uses your data scope.
**Day of month** can be 1 to 28, so the report runs in every month.

sections.title: Manage scheduled reports
sections.intro: Test, change, pause or delete a scheduled report, and see past deliveries.
prerequisites: You have the **Schedule report delivery** permission.
steps: Select **Analytics**, then the **Scheduled** tab.
To see past deliveries, select **History** on the schedule.
Select the schedule's menu (**...**).
Select **Run now** to send the report at once. Use it to test a new schedule.
Select **Edit** to change the schedule. Select **Save** in the dialog.
Select **Pause** to stop deliveries for a while. Select **Resume** to start them again.
sections.result: The schedule shows **Active** or **Paused**, its next run and its last run.

blocks.caption: The Scheduled tab with two scheduled reports.
blocks.alt: Scheduled tab with numbered highlights on New schedule, a schedule, History and the schedule menu

callouts: A schedule with its status, format, report, frequency, period, recipients, owner and next run.
The schedule menu: **Run now**, **Edit**, **Pause** or **Resume**, and **Delete**.

blocks.caption: The delivery history of a schedule.
blocks.alt: Delivery history panel with a succeeded delivery, its time, recipients and file

blocks.warning: **Delete** stops the deliveries and removes the delivery history.

sections.title: Rebuild the figures
sections.intro: If figures look out of date, ask the app to rebuild them from the tickets.
prerequisites: You have the **View team, department and organisation analytics** permission.
steps: On any **Analytics** tab, select the **...** button at the top right.
Select **Rebuild metrics from tickets**.
sections.result: A message says **Rebuild queued** or **Metrics are current**. It shows how many tickets have figures and how many are missing or out of date.

troubleshooting.problem: The page says **Personal analytics** and shows only your tickets.
troubleshooting.cause: You do not have team analytics.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator for the **View team, department and organisation analytics** permission.

troubleshooting.problem: A widget or report says **No data**.
troubleshooting.cause: Nothing matches the period and filters.
troubleshooting.fix: Choose a longer period or remove some filters.

troubleshooting.problem: The **Scheduled** or **Exports** tab is missing, or says it is not available.
troubleshooting.cause: Your role lacks the schedule or export permission.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator for **Schedule report delivery** or **Export reports (CSV/Excel/PDF)**.

troubleshooting.cause: The file could not be built or fetched.
troubleshooting.fix: Try again. If it keeps failing, export a shorter period.
Open the **Exports** tab later and select **Download**.

troubleshooting.problem: Saving a schedule shows a red message under a field.
troubleshooting.cause: A value is missing or not allowed, such as a wrong e-mail address or time zone.
troubleshooting.fix: Correct the field. Use a time zone name such as `Asia/Kolkata`.

troubleshooting.cause: Some ticket figures have not been calculated yet.
troubleshooting.fix: Select **...** > **Rebuild metrics from tickets**, or ask a supervisor to do it.

faq.q: Why do my numbers differ from a colleague's?
faq.a: Each person sees only the tickets in their data scope. A team lead may see one team, and a manager the whole organisation.

faq.q: Can I build my own report?
faq.a: No. Use the ten standard reports with filters, or build a dashboard with your own widgets.

faq.q: Whose data does a scheduled report contain?
faq.a: It uses the data scope of the person who owns the schedule. Recipients see what the owner would see.

faq.q: What does (bh) mean next to a time?
faq.a: Business hours. Nights, weekends and holidays outside business hours are not counted.

glossary.definition: A page of widgets that show support figures, charts and tables.
One figure, chart or table on a dashboard.
Selecting a figure, bar or row to see the tickets behind it.
The tickets your role lets you see: your own, your team's, your department's or the whole organisation's.
The share of tickets solved with the first reply, without further back and forth.
Working hours set by your administrator. Times marked (bh) count only these hours.
A standard report that is e-mailed as an attachment on a regular day and time.
